status_reason: The concept cannot be approved: the existing Vis-NIR silica cable does not transmit the mid-IR, no documented mid-IR fiber reach covers a link to another building, and the link length, routing and conditions needed for any approval are not supplied.
answer: No, the concept cannot be approved as stated, because a Vis-NIR silica cable transmits only about 350-2400 nm while MIR ATR water-in-oil spectra lie at 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 µm) and need chalcogenide (CIR) or polycrystalline (PIR) fibers. MIR ATR itself is worth testing first because AFS slides show ATR spectra of oil with 0.1-2.0 % water, but the sources document long 100-300 m cables only for silica, so the analyzer distance must be confirmed by AFS. NIR on the existing silica cable is the alternative to compare, since NIR suits remote fiber probes and moisture bands lie in the NIR.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR with a ZrO2 or diamond ATR probe on CIR/PIR fiber for water in petroleum, compared with NIR on the existing silica cable
inline.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 (or diamond) tip sealed in a PEEK shaft
inline.install: In the petroleum line close to an FTIR analyzer, because no long mid-IR link is documented
inline.fiber: Chalcogenide CIR (1.1-6.5 µm, covers 4000-2000 cm-1) or PIR (3-17 µm, covers only below about 3333 cm-1); not the existing Vis-NIR silica cable
inline.test_against: NIR transmission/transflection probe on the existing low-OH Vis-NIR silica cable
inline.not_final_because: The published petroleum example is a laboratory slide without detection limit, link length or process conditions, the mid-IR fiber reach to another building is undocumented, and line conditions, water range and reference method are unknown.

problems.text: The existing visible/NIR silica cable (about 350-2400 nm) cannot carry MIR ATR, whose water-in-oil spectra span 4000-2000 cm-1 (2.5-5 µm); mid-IR needs CIR (1.1-6.5 µm) or PIR (3-17 µm) fibers.

Placing the analyzer in another building is not documented for MIR: 100-300 m cables are described only for low-OH silica, and the PIR versus hollow-waveguide comparison is shown for 2 m lengths, so AFS must confirm whether any MIR link of the required length is feasible.
Approval is asked before the facts allow it: fiber type, link length, routing and operating conditions are not supplied, and method selection depends on such factors.
The petroleum ATR example is a reason to test MIR ATR, not proof: the slide gives no detection limit, fiber link length or process conditions.

methods.why: Same measured quantity is shown on AFS slides (oil with 0.1-2.0 % water, 4000-2000 cm-1) and MIR ATR suits liquids with high selectivity, but needs CIR/PIR fiber.
NIR works with ordinary glass optics and remote fiber probes, moisture bands lie at 1.3-2.2 µm within the Vis-NIR silica range, and long silica cables exist, so it could reuse the existing cable.
Raman is recorded in the visible/NIR on silica fibers and carries information complementary to MIR, but signals are weak and often masked by fluorescence of organic compounds.
Fluorimetry relies on secondary emission of certain substances and has low selectivity, so it is not a direct route to water content.

questions.q: What is the cable length and routing from the sampling point in the line to the analyzer building?
questions.why: Long cables are documented only for silica, and MIR fiber reach must be confirmed by AFS.

questions.q: What are the temperature, pressure, flow and cleaning conditions at the sampling point?
questions.why: Probe construction (ZrO2/diamond tip in PEEK) and method selection depend on such factors.

questions.q: What water content range must be measured and with what accuracy?
questions.why: The AFS example covers 0.1-2.0 % water only and states no detection limit.

questions.q: Which independent laboratory analysis can provide reference water values for the samples?
questions.why: Quantitative use requires chemometric calibration models that are built and validated against reference data.

questions.q: Is the water dissolved, emulsified or present as separate droplets or layers?
questions.why: ATR samples only a thin layer of 1-6 µm, so heterogeneity at the probe surface affects what is measured.

experiment.objective: Check in the laboratory whether MIR ATR and NIR see the water content differences in the client's petroleum, before any in-line concept is approved.
steps: Collect client petroleum samples covering the expected water range, each with an independent laboratory water analysis.
Measure the samples with a ZrO2 or diamond ATR probe on CIR/PIR fiber coupled to an FTIR spectrometer.
Measure the same samples with an NIR transmission/transflection probe on Vis-NIR silica fiber.
Identify key spectral features and build and validate a chemometric model for each method against the reference values.
Ask AFS to confirm the feasible MIR fiber length and compare it with the client's link length.
references: Independent laboratory water-content analysis of each sample (method to be named by the client)

pathway.key_features: No client spectra are given; the AFS example shows ATR absorbance in 4000-2000 cm-1 increasing with water content from 0.1 to 2.0 %.
pathway.path_reason: The multi-method lab test and key-feature selection must come before choosing a chemometric model, customised system or sensor.

multispectral.why: Oil is named among complex media that may need two or more methods, and MIR gives well-defined absorption peaks while NIR gives broad overtone bands and suits long remote fibers.
multispectral.probe: separate synchronised probes, unless the water is heterogeneously distributed, in which case a same-spot multispectral probe is needed (a four-method MIR/NIR/Raman/fluorescence probe is only under development)
multispectral.fusion: model per method first, then a dedicated data-fusion model of synchronised spectra
multispectral.test: The fused model must predict the reference water values better than the best single-method model on the same validation data.

assumptions: The target is water content in a liquid petroleum stream at a single sampling point in the line.
The existing silica cable is a Vis-NIR silica fiber transmitting about 350-2400 nm.
